svg.title: French bread names: which are protected by law and what each requires
svg.desc: Four protected names and one group of free names. Pain de tradition française (décret 93-1074, article 2): wheat flour, drinking water and salt only; baker's yeast and/or levain; optional bean flour up to 2 percent, soy flour up to 0.5 percent and wheat malt flour up to 0.3 percent of the total flour; no additive; no freezing during making. Pain maison (article 1): kneaded, shaped and baked entirely where it is sold. Au levain (articles 3 and 4): crumb pH 4.3 or less and at least 900 ppm acetic acid; baker's yeast only at the final mixing, at most 0.2 percent of the flour used at that stage. Boulanger and boulangerie (Code de la consommation L122-17): kneading, fermentation, shaping and baking done on site from chosen raw materials; dough and bread never frozen at any stage of production or sale. Free names with no legal recipe: pain courant, pain de campagne, pain complet and other descriptive mentions; they must not mislead the customer (L121-2). Names combine: a tradition au levain must meet both sets of rules.

g.text: French bread names: what the law protects
Checked on Légifrance 2026-10-08. Protected names in colour; free names in grey.
Pain de tradition française
décret n°93-1074, article 2
• Dough of wheat flour, drinking water, salt only
• Fermented with baker's yeast and/or levain
• Optional, as % of the total flour:
bean flour ≤ 2 % · soy flour ≤ 0.5 % · wheat malt flour ≤ 0.3 %
• No additive at all (no E300, no improver)
• No freezing (surgélation) during making
Cold retarding above 0 °C is allowed.
Pain maison
décret n°93-1074, article 1
• Kneaded, shaped and baked entirely
at the place where it is sold to the customer
« Au levain »
articles 3 and 4
• Crumb pH ≤ 4.3 and ≥ 900 ppm acetic acid
• Baker's yeast only at the final mixing,
at most 0.2 % of the flour used at that stage
« Boulanger » and the sign « Boulangerie »
Code de la consommation, article L122-17
• The business itself kneads, ferments and shapes the dough from chosen raw materials, and bakes on the site of sale
• Dough and bread never frozen (surgelés or congelés) at any stage of production or sale
No legal recipe: pain courant, pain de campagne, pain complet, « multi-céréales »…
• Composition and method chosen by the baker; additives allowed for bread may be used (not in tradition)
• The name must not mislead about composition or method (Code de la consommation L121-2)
• Pain courant must also respect the salt limit (1.4 g per 100 g of bread, lesson 02.5)
Names add up, rules add up
A « tradition au levain maison » must meet article 2 AND articles 3-4 AND article 1. Fail one rule and that word comes off the label.
Label Rouge « Baguette de tradition française » (LA 22/01) is a voluntary label with its own extra specification.
